page: Vultr vc2-1c-2gb is an entry-tier virtual machine belonging to the Cloud Compute family. It operates on the x86_64 architecture using a single shared Intel Xeon vCPU clocked at 2.0 GHz, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is provisioned at 2.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation. Storage consists of a bundled 55 GB local NVMe SSD, accompanied by one complimentary public IPv4 address. The configuration includes no discrete graphics processing hardware.

Benchmark results situate the compute and memory subsystem in the lower performance brackets. The single shared vCPU achieved a PassMark CPU score of 1141.0 and a stress-ng score of 1211.89, placing it in the bottom decile for multi-core compute and bottom quartile for single-core execution. Memory throughput registered 85.9 GB/sec for small cached reads, falling to 7.23 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 5.37 GB/sec for uncached writes. Under application-level benchmarks, the instance sustained 0.67 million Redis SET operations per second and 0.78 GB/sec in static web throughput, while single-threaded gzip compression reached 20.76 GB/sec.

With its shared CPU allocation and modest footprint, vc2-1c-2gb provides an economical compute profile for light operations where high thread density or dedicated compute cycles are unnecessary. The inclusion of fast NVMe local storage offsets the conservative CPU capabilities by delivering rapid disk access. It is appropriate for staging environments, low-traffic web endpoints, microservices, light cron jobs, and basic development tasks.
